title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's theory of basic localizers (Pursuing Stacks / 'Les Dérivateurs' circle, 1983 onward).

- W is a basic localizer on (Cat).
- For a small category A, A^ denotes presheaves on A, and i_A : A^ -> Cat sends X to A/X.
- W_A = i_A^{-1}(W) is the induced class of weak equivalences in A^, with Hot_A = W_A^{-1} A^.
- An object or category is 'W-aspherical' if its map to the point is in W.

The page finishes an equivalence theorem begun on the previous pages, about when A^ -> Hot(W) commutes with products.

Step 1: reducing (iv). It is already known that Cat -> Hot(W) commutes with finite products, since finite products of maps in W are in W. So condition (iv), 'A^ -> Hot(W) commutes with binary products', means: for all X, Y in A^ the canonical functor u : A/(X×Y) -> A/X × A/Y is in W.

Step 2: necessity. Take X = a and Y = b representable. Then A/a and A/b have final objects, so the target is contractible. Hence (iv) forces A/(a×b) to be W-aspherical, i.e. every product a×b of representables in A^ is W-aspherical. This is the defining condition of A being totally W-aspherical, once A itself is aspherical.

Step 3: sufficiency, in a stronger form. Suppose all a×b are aspherical. Then u is a W-aspherical functor, i.e. all its comma categories over objects of the target are aspherical, and so u ∈ W by the Quillen Theorem A axiom of basic localizers. Proof: for α = (a->X, b->Y) in A/X × A/Y, an object of the comma category is c -> X×Y together with maps c -> a over X and c -> b over Y. That is exactly a map c -> a×b. Hence (A/(X×Y))/α ≅ A/(a×b), which is aspherical.

Step 4: summary diagram.
- (i) A totally W-aspherical ⇔ (iv) A^ -> Hot(W) commutes with binary products ⇔ (iv bis) commutes with finite products.
- These are linked by ⇑⇓ to (ii) W_A stable under finite products ⇔ (iii bis) f ∈ W_A ⇒ f × id_X ∈ W_A for all X.
- These in turn imply (iii) A^ -> Hot_A commutes with finite products.
- The margin bracket, 'i_A ... W-asph.', apparently recalls that i_A is W-aspherical, so Hot_A -> Hot(W) is an equivalence when A is aspherical.

Purpose: characterize totally aspherical categories, a step in the theory of (strict) test categories, by compatibility of the localization with products.
errors: 'A^ tot. W-asph.' is a slip of the pen: the condition is on A (all a×b aspherical in A^, together with asphericity of A), not on A^. This is consistent with the summary line '(i) A tot. W-asph.'

The full equivalence (i) ⇔ (iv) tacitly needs A to be W-aspherical (included in the definition of totally aspherical, or forced by X = Y = final object). The page only checks the a×b condition. The previous page did make the asphericity caveat explicit for (i) ⇔ (ii).
The comma-category identification is stated without detail but is correct.

ideas.what: Totally aspherical category A characterized by A/(X×Y) -> A/X × A/Y being in W (indeed W-aspherical) for all presheaves X, Y, i.e. i_A commutes with finite products up to W
ideas.modern_name: totally aspherical small category; product compatibility of i_A: A^ -> Cat
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, 1983), developed by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks, sections on totally aspherical / strict test categories

ideas.what: Comma category identification (A/(X×Y))/(a/X, b/Y) ≅ A/(a×b), combined with Quillen's Theorem A for basic localizers
ideas.modern_name: W-aspherical functor via slice computation (Theorem A)

ideas.what: Equivalence of: W_A stable under finite products; f ∈ W_A ⇒ f×id_X ∈ W_A; A^ -> Hot_A commutes with finite products
ideas.modern_name: strict test category / Hot_A compatible with products (product-stability of weak equivalences)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the characterization of totally aspherical categories via product-compatibility of i_A, which appears in Pursuing Stacks and is systematized by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski. The argument is correct and standard. Nothing new is apparent.
